mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within three months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic output and corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 2% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market uncertainty decreases.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% each over three months signals a broad-based strengthening of demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity accelerates.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both increase > 2% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both RSAFS and HOUST increase by more than 2% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with an increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over a quarter signals a supportive monetary policy in a growing economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic activity improve.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases and GDPC1 increases > 1% in 1 quarter
regime_hint: economic expansion with accommodative monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS decreases and GDPC1 increases by more than 1% within a quarter.
